subject: Can I store a graph created with viewport into a ggplot object?

messages.author: f2c49605155dcc5b
messages.subject: Can I store a graph created with viewport into a ggplot object?
parts:
Hi there,

I have a class of objects to which I assigned a slot of type (class)
"ggplot." Single or faceted plots can be stored in the slot, since
these are of class ggplot. But the only way I know to generate
subplots is with viewports, which affect directly the active device.
Is there a means to combine two ggplot objects into one so that the
result mimics subplotting via the viewport?

Here's a simple example of what I'm looking for - using the viewport:
bb1<-ggplot(full.ts, aes(x=bin, y=full.ts[,2]), height=2) +
geom_bar(stat="identity") + ...
bb2<-ggplot(full.ts, aes(x=bin*bz, y=full.ts[,3]), height=2) +
geom_bar(stat="identity") + coord_polar() + ...
grid.newpage()
pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(3,2))
print(bb2, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 1:2, layout.pos.col
= 1:2))
print(bb1, vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = 3, layout.pos.col =
1:2))

Using ggplot? (e.g., call the function ggplot_viewport)
bb1<-ggplot(full.ts, aes(x=bin, y=full.ts[,2]), height=2) +
geom_bar(stat="identity") + ...
bb2<-ggplot(full.ts, aes(x=bin*bz, y=full.ts[,3]), height=2) +
geom_bar(stat="identity") + coord_polar() + ...
grid.newpage()
bb3<-ggplot_viewport(layout = grid.layout(3,2) + layout(bb1, pos.row =
1:2, pos.col=1:2) +
layout(bb2, pos.row = 3, pos.col=1:2))

Is this currently possible with ggplot?

Many thanks for any help.

Leo

messages.subject: Re: Can I store a graph created with viewport into a ggplot object?
parts:
Hi Leo,

It sounds like you need to create your own class that captures this
information - a main plot, plus a list of subplots and their viewport
information.

Hadley
